findings.title: Preserve a late PREPARE terminal result after the production timeout
findings.trigger: PREPARE_CODING exceeds its unchanged 45000ms timer; valid original RESULT arrives later while the native process and host stay unchanged.
findings.observed: onLine clears pending and resolves an already rejected promise. prepareCoding never validates or stores the late request_id/request_hash. The retained operation stays PREPARE_UNRESOLVED without identity. STATUS throws CODING_PREPARE_ORIGINAL_UNRESOLVED and another PREPARE throws CODING_ORIGINAL_REQUEST_PENDING.
findings.impact: An ordinary slow preparation permanently blocks coding setup for this Desktop manager even after an authoritative late result is available; the original request cannot be reconciled.
findings.repair: Give the retained original operation a terminal-reply handler independent of the caller promise; validate and adopt the original late result exactly once before clearing the shared pending barrier. Keep invalid or host-mismatched replies quarantined.

findings.title: Settle an authoritative PREPARE rejection so corrected input can retry
findings.trigger: The private host responds to PREPARE_CODING with valid ERROR/MANAGEMENT_REJECTED, such as a missing source path before any intent is created.
findings.observed: The explicit rejection throws CODING_PREPARE_REJECTED but leaves the newly created no-ID PREPARE_UNRESOLVED operation active. All later PREPARE and STATUS calls fail as in finding 001.
findings.impact: A recoverable preparation input error requires a manager restart instead of allowing corrected paths; no ambiguity remains in this proven rejected case.
findings.repair: Represent a validated authoritative PREPARE rejection as a terminal nonaccepted operation, retain its audit information, and permit corrected PREPARE only after the shared barrier is clear. Do not treat timeout or malformed replies as rejection.

findings.title: Recheck synchronous consent guards after the final awaited recheck returns
findings.trigger: After the second recheckCodingConsent finishes its internal checks, a queued context-change microtask runs before confirmCoding resumes from await.
findings.observed: The finally block clears consentPending and confirmCoding consumes/sends CONFIRM_CODING without checking current selection again. Synthetic fixture switches session-1 to session-2 in this exact microtask window and records one CONFIRM for session-1 followed by CODING_CONFIGURED.
findings.impact: A user selection changed before send can still commit the old session scope. The comment claiming no await between final guard and write overlooks the outer await boundary.
findings.qualification: Deterministic synthetic event ordering injected via observeProcess callback; no claim that a native GUI race was exercised. All candidate methods and bound modules are unchanged.
findings.repair: After the final await, synchronously verify active intent, no pending command, consent ownership, context/selection/resource generation, native host/process identity and expiry immediately before marking confirmSent and writing. Share the synchronous guard with recheckCodingConsent; do not add another await between it and exchange.

original_findings.evidence: Main IPC now requires privileged callback; direct invocation with cancel prompts once and sends zero CONFIRM. Native dialog implementation reviewed, not shown interactively.
Expired intent is retained while STATUS is pending and same original receives late status.
PREPARE result retains request ID on context change; returning to original selection can STATUS without another PREPARE.

Chromium STATUS recovery followed by one failed refresh and successful retry: confirms1, refreshes1, attempts2; repeated STATUS/remount do not duplicate successful refresh. NativeWorkbench parent callback reviewed, not full end-to-end V2 transport exercised.
